title: Terraform VPC Service-Chain Orchestrator: subnet scheduling, NAT/IGW HA, endpoints, routing and upgrade probes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a composable Terraform module that acts as a VPC 'service-chain orchestrator' for private deployments. The module must provision subnet groups (control/data/infra), attach HA-capable NAT and IGW constructs, create and manage AWS interface and gateway VPC endpoints, and reconcile route tables with intent-driven routing policies. It must include preflight validation, in-plan safety checks, and an upgrade orchestration layer that supports canary upgrades of route tables and NAT replacements with automatic health probes and rollback hooks. Target customers are Dedicated and Private deployments that require predictable egress, regulatory isolation, and safe upgrade windows.
acceptance_criteria: Module outputs documented variables, resource IDs, and a minimal example to wire into private control plane stacks.
Supports multi-AZ subnet group creation with subnet tagging and deterministic placement across AZs.
Implements HA NAT architecture: active/standby NAT instances or managed NAT gateways per AZ with configurable failover policy.
Creates interface endpoints and S3/Dynamo gateway endpoints as configurable lists; automatically attaches route table entries where appropriate.
Provides an 'upgrade_mode' that can be 'manual', 'canary', or 'rolling', and a canary flow that replaces NAT/route table entries in a single AZ and runs health probes before proceeding.
Health-checking subsystem runs synthetic egress probes (HTTP/S and TCP) and reports failures as terraform plan warnings and results in automatic rollback in canary mode.
Includes drift detection helpers (lightweight terraform external data script) that surface unexpected route/endpoint changes to the ops console.
Automated unit and integration tests (local terraform test + terratest or equivalent) exist and pass in the staging account.
Security review completed and KMS/SSM secrets usage is documented in the module README.
Example overlay shows how to pin module version and run a canary upgrade using CI job template (circleci/github-actions).

notes: Implementation choices: prefer managed NAT by default; expose nat_mode variable (managed|instance) so regulated customers can provide hardened instances.

The canary replacement flow uses a 3-step swap: provision replacement resources in AZ -> run pre-swap probes against replacement egress IPs -> swap route table entries and run post-swap probes -> mark canary healthy or rollback.
To keep terraform idempotent, we model route-table swaps as create-new-route + wait-for-probe + remove-old-route (not in-place update).

Drift detection will use a lightweight lambda triggered by schedule to compare live route/endpoint state against TF state stored in SSM parameter or a known state bucket and open an ops incident via webhook if divergence > threshold.
Future work: add support for cross-account VPC endpoints for shared services and a UI knob in Console to trigger module-driven canary upgrades.
